title: Area of Triangle using 1/2 ab sin C - Problems

problems.problem_text: A triangle has two sides of lengths 6 cm and 8 cm with an included angle of 30 degrees. Find the area of the triangle.
Calculate the area of a triangle with sides 10 cm and 12 cm and an included angle of 45 degrees. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
Find the area of a triangle with sides 5 cm and 9 cm and an included angle of 60 degrees.
A triangle has sides of 7 cm and 11 cm with an included angle of 90 degrees. Find its area.
A triangle has two sides of lengths 8 cm and 12 cm with an included angle of 50 degrees. Find the area, correct to 2 decimal places.
A triangle has area 30 sq cm and two sides of lengths 8 cm and 10 cm. Find the included angle between these sides, correct to 1 decimal place.
A triangle has area 25 sq cm, one side of length 5 cm, and an included angle of 30 degrees. Find the length of the other side that forms the angle.
Find the area of a triangle with sides 9 cm and 14 cm and an included angle of 65 degrees. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
A triangle has area 40 sq cm and two sides of lengths 10 cm and 12 cm. Find the possible values of the included angle between these sides, correct to 1 decimal place.
problems.solution: Area = (1/2) * 10 * 12 * sin(C) = 60 * sin(C). 40 = 60 * sin(C). sin(C) = 40/60 = 2/3 = 0.6667. C = sin^-1(0.6667) = 41.8 degrees. Since sin(180 - C) = sin(C), C could also be 180 - 41.8 = 138.2 degrees.

problems.problem_text: Calculate the area of a triangle with sides 6 cm and 10 cm and an included angle of 40 degrees. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
A triangle has area 36 sq cm, one side of length 9 cm, and the included angle between this side and the unknown side is 55 degrees. Find the length of the unknown side, correct to 2 decimal places.
Find the area of a triangle with sides 15 cm and 20 cm and an included angle of 35 degrees. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

In triangle ABC, side a = 12 cm, side b = 15 cm, and side c = 10 cm. Find the area of the triangle using the formula (1/2)ab sin C. First find angle C using the cosine rule. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
In triangle ABC, angle A = 40 degrees, side b = 20 cm, and side c = 25 cm. Find the area of the triangle, correct to 2 decimal places.
In triangle PQR, side p = 14 cm, side q = 18 cm, and the area is 100 sq cm. Find the included angle R between sides p and q, correct to 1 decimal place.

In triangle ABC, sides a = 13 cm, b = 14 cm, and c = 15 cm. Find the area of the triangle. (Hint: Use cosine rule to find one angle, then use area formula.) Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
